title: Create a `Map<Long, String>` of employee id → employee name.
shortTitle: Create a Map<Long, String> of employee id to employee name
keyPoints: Collectors.toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper) builds a Map by applying two functions to each element
Employee::getId as the key and Employee::getName as the value creates an id-to-name lookup
The two-argument toMap throws IllegalStateException on duplicate keys, which surfaces data integrity issues
The three-argument form with a merge function resolves duplicate keys explicitly
toMap rejects null values by throwing NullPointerException
The default map is HashMap; use the four-argument form with a map supplier for ordering or a specific type

s1_definition.oneliner: Collectors.toMap(Employee::getId, Employee::getName) turns a list of employees into an id-to-name lookup map.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Collectors.toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper)** builds a `Map` by applying a key function and a value function to each stream element.
- **Employee::getId** extracts the key; **Employee::getName** extracts the value.
- **Duplicate keys** cause `IllegalStateException` with the two-argument form.
- **Null values** cause `NullPointerException` because the internal merge logic uses Map.merge.
- The default implementation is **HashMap**; use the four-argument form for a specific type.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India has a pile of employee files and wants a quick phone-book style index: give an employee id and get back the name. She makes an index card for each employee where the id is the label and the name is the content.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Stream<Employee>
  [1001:Rajesh, 1002:Priya, 1003:Amit]
       │
       │  Collectors.toMap(getId, getName)
       ▼
  For each element:
    1001 → "Rajesh"   (insert)
    1002 → "Priya"    (insert)
    1003 → "Amit"     (insert)
       │
       ▼
  Map<Long, String>
  ┌──────────────────────┐
  │  1001 → "Rajesh"     │
  │  1002 → "Priya"      │
  │  1003 → "Amit"       │
  └──────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To build an id-to-name lookup, collect the employee stream with Collectors.toMap, passing Employee::getId as the key mapper and Employee::getName as the value mapper. The result is a HashMap giving constant-time lookups by id.

Because ids are supposed to be unique, each key appears exactly once. If two employees share an id, the two-argument toMap throws an IllegalStateException, which is a feature: it surfaces a data integrity problem instead of silently dropping a record. When duplicates are expected, supply a merge function in the three-argument form.

Be deliberate about nulls and map type: toMap throws NPE on null values, and HashMap has no ordering. Use the four-argument form with a TreeMap or LinkedHashMap supplier when you need sorted keys or insertion order.

Remember one sentence: toMap(keyMapper, valueMapper) builds a one-to-one lookup map, and the two-argument form deliberately throws on duplicate keys to enforce uniqueness.
